intro: 気 is your attention and inner mood, treated as a thing that can be heavy, scattered, pointed somewhere or put to use. The particle after 気 tells you who is in control: with 気が and 気に something happens in your mind by itself, and with 気を (and 気にする) you do it on purpose. Learn each expression as one fixed unit, particle included.

skills.rule: 気が/気に + verb: it happens to you (気がする, 気がつく, 気になる, 気に入る, 気が合う); 気を/気にする: you do it (気をつける, 気にする).
skills.explain:
Things that happen to you. 気がする 'have a feeling that' follows a clause, often with ような: 誰かいるような気がする. Xに気がつく (= 気づく) 'notice X'. Xが気になる: X nags at you, makes you curious or uneasy, without your choosing. Xが気に入る 'take a liking to X', usually 気に入った or 気に入っている. Xと気が合う 'get on well with X'.

Things you do. Xに気をつける 'be careful of X', mostly as a request: 気をつけて. Xを気にする 'worry about, mind X'; 気にしないで 'never mind, don't worry'.

The two trap pairs. 気がつく (notice) and 気をつける (take care) both take に; only the particle after 気 separates them. 気になる (it bothers me) and 気にする (I let it bother me): only 気にする can be asked not to, so 'don't worry about it' is 気にしないで. Finally, 気に入る is for a particular thing you have met or chosen; general tastes are 好き.
patterns: [clause] (ような) 気がする — I have a feeling that ...
[thing] が 気になる — it nags at me, I'm curious about it
[thing] を 気にする — worry about, mind
[danger] に 気をつける — be careful of
[fact] に 気がつく — notice, realise
[thing] が 気に入る — take a liking to
[person] と 気が合う — get on well with

examples.jp: 足元[あしもと]に{気[き]をつけて}ください。
この部屋[へや]、とても{気[き]に入[い]りました}。
山田[やまだ]さんとは不思議[ふしぎ]と{気[き]が合[あ]う}。
examples.en: Strangely enough, I get on well with Yamada-san.

examples.jp: 駅[えき]で財布[さいふ]がないことに{気[き]がつきました}。
examples.en: At the station I noticed my wallet was gone.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]は雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るような{気[き]がします}。
examples.en: I have a feeling it will rain tomorrow.

examples.jp: テストの結果[けっか]が{気[き]になって}、眠[ねむ]れません。
examples.en: I keep thinking about the test results and can't sleep.

contrast.vs: 気になる ↔ 気にする
contrast.note: 気になる is involuntary and the thing takes が: 音が気になる 'the noise bothers me'. 気にする is a choice and the thing takes を: 音を気にしないで 'don't let the noise bother you'.

contrast.vs: 気がつく ↔ 気をつける
contrast.note: Notice versus be careful. 気がついた 'I realised'; 気をつけて 'take care'. Both mark the thing with に, so look only at が or を after 気.
好き is a general taste (寿司が好き). 気に入る is taking to a specific thing you have just met or chosen: このセーター、気に入った.

mistakes.bad: 車[くるま]に{気[き]がついて}ください。
mistakes.good: 車[くるま]に{気[き]をつけて}ください。
mistakes.note: 'Watch out for cars' is 気をつける. 気がつく means notice and is not used to warn someone.

mistakes.bad: 遅[おく]れたことは{気[き]にならないで}ください。
mistakes.good: 遅[おく]れたことは{気[き]にしないで}ください。
mistakes.note: 気になる is not under your control, so nobody can be asked not to do it. 'Don't worry about it' is 気にしないで.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]はテニスが{気[き]に入[い]ります}。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]はテニスが{好[す]きです}。
mistakes.note: A general liking is 好き. 気に入る is for a particular thing, and is mostly 気に入った or 気に入っている.

skills.tip: Look at the particle after 気: が or に, it happens to you; を, or 気にする, you do it.

skills.rule: Picture 気 as an object: heavy 気が重い, light 気が楽, short 気が短い, working 気が利く, scattered 気が散る, settled 気が済む, pointed 気が向く, spent on others 気を遣う.
skills.explain:
Almost all of these take 気が; only 気を遣う has を, because you deliberately spend your 気 on other people.

Mood: 気が重い 'dread, feel weighed down' about something ahead (会議を思うと気が重い). Its opposite is 気が楽 'at ease, relieved', usually 気が楽になる. 気が向く 'feel like doing', mostly 気が向いたら and 気が向かない. 気が済む 'feel satisfied, get it out of your system', mostly 気が済むまで and ～ないと気が済まない.

Character: 気が短い 'impatient, quick-tempered' (opposite 気が長い). 気が利く 'thoughtful, quick to see what is needed'; 気が利かない is a common criticism.

Attention: 気が散る 'be distracted', the cause marked で.

気を遣う 'be considerate, go out of your way for others' is also written 気を使う. 気を遣わないでください means 'please don't go to any trouble'.
patterns: [thought of something ahead] と 気が重い — dread
[after relief] 気が楽になる — feel relieved
気が短い / 気が長い — impatient / patient (a trait)
[noise] で 気が散る — be distracted
[action] ないと 気が済まない / 気が済むまで — not satisfied until
気が向いたら / 気が向かない — if I feel like it / not in the mood
[person] に 気を遣う — be considerate of, take pains for

examples.jp: 全部[ぜんぶ]話[はな]したら、{気[き]が楽[らく]になりました}。
examples.en: Once I'd told them everything, I felt much better.

examples.jp: 明日[あした]の面接[めんせつ]のことを考[かんが]えると、{気[き]が重[おも]い}。
examples.en: Thinking about tomorrow's interview fills me with dread.

examples.jp: {気[き]が向[む]いたら}、また連絡[れんらく]してください。
examples.en: Get in touch again if you feel like it.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんは本当[ほんとう]に{気[き]が利[き]く}人[ひと]ですね。
examples.en: Tanaka-san is really thoughtful, isn't she?

examples.jp: 妻[つま]の両親[りょうしん]の前[まえ]では、いつも{気[き]を遣[つか]います}。
examples.en: I'm always on my best behaviour around my wife's parents.

examples.jp: 自分[じぶん]で確[たし]かめないと{気[き]が済[す]まない}。
examples.en: I'm never satisfied until I've checked for myself.

contrast.vs: 気が利く ↔ 気を遣う
contrast.note: 気が利く praises a knack for doing the right thing unasked. 気を遣う is effort spent on others' feelings and can be tiring: 気を遣って疲れた. Both earn thanks: 気を遣ってくれてありがとう.
Opposite ends of one scale: dread of something ahead versus relief or ease once the weight is gone.

contrast.vs: 気が向く ↔ 気が済む
contrast.note: 気が向く is before the act: do you feel like starting? 気が済む is after: do you feel it is done? Hence 気が向いたら but 気が済むまで.

mistakes.bad: 父[ちち]は{気[き]が重[おも]くて}、すぐ怒[おこ]ります。
mistakes.good: 父[ちち]は{気[き]が短[みじか]くて}、すぐ怒[おこ]ります。
mistakes.note: A quick temper is 気が短い. 気が重い is dread about something coming, not a character trait.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]のことは{気[き]が利[き]かないで}ください。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]のことは{気[き]を遣[つか]わないで}ください。
mistakes.note: 気が利く describes a trait, not something you can ask someone to stop. 'Don't go to any trouble for me' is 気を遣わないで.

mistakes.bad: 音楽[おんがく]がうるさくて{気[き]が向[む]きません}。
mistakes.good: 音楽[おんがく]がうるさくて{気[き]が散[ち]ります}。
mistakes.note: Noise breaking your concentration is 気が散る. 気が向かない means you are not in the mood.

skills.tip: Ask what is happening to the 気: weighed down, lightened, cut short, put to work, scattered, settled, pointed or spent.
